This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine glucose tests, potentially leading to false results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes. Laboratory and/or medical tests, such as complete blood counts and kidney or liver function tests, may be conducted while you are using this medication. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, it is crucial to contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage instructions, refer to the product guidelines or consult your pharmacist. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not encompass all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for comprehensive information about this product and your individual health needs. This medication is administered via injection into a muscle or vein as directed by your doctor, typically every 6 to 8 hours. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure you have been thoroughly trained by a healthcare professional on its preparation and usage. Inspect the product visually for particles or discoloration before use; do not use the liquid if either is present. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed treatment course, even if symptoms resolve after a few days. Common side effects may include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site. Rarely, this medication may cause stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. In rare cases, this medication may lead to a severe intestinal condition caused by the bacteria Clostridium difficile. This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has ceased. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. Before using imipenem with cilastatin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to either of its components, other carbapenems (e.g., meropenem), penicillins, cephalosporins, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is also excreted into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete and personalized information about this medication and your specific health needs.
